newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan recovery trend goes on despite tax rise--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan recovery trend goes on despite tax rise--BOJ.

text.p: The Japanese economy is continuing on a gradual recovery trend supported by firm production and incomes despite a lingering impact from the increase in the consumption tax, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a meeting of the central bank's branch managers on Monday.
Public-sector investment is on a declining trend but net exports are continuing to increase, Matsushita said in a statement.
Although there is a lingering impact on private consumption from the April 1 rise in the sales tax, the employment and income situation is still gradually improving, he said.
"There is little possibility that the recovery trend itself with falter," Matsushita said in the statement.
He said corporate capital spending is steadily increasing, helped by rising profits, especially among major firms.
"On the production side, the drop since the spring is likely to be limited to a small one," he said.

A positive cyclical mechanism in the private-sector economy continues to function. "The slowdown in the economy now will be temporary, and there is a high possibility that the economy will continue its recovery. However, we must keep sufficient watch over these points, including the speed of the recovery," he said.

Prices are generally stable if one excludes the impact from the rise in the consumption tax. "Monetary policy management for now will put emphasis on making the basis for economic recovery firmer while keeping close watch over developments," he said.
Matsushita said financial institutions are continuing to actively cope with their problem loans, and the matter is being addressed steadily.
It is important for financial institutions to quickly dispose of their problem loans in the face of reforms in the financial and capital markets, he said.

"The various scandals over financial institutions are basically illegal acts of individual organisations. However, the BOJ strongly hopes that through clarifying facts and efforts to renew management structures they will be able to recover credibility as soon as possible both at home and abroad," he said.
The BOJ plans to push for stronger risk management and better internal management systems in financial institutions through its inspections, Matsushita said.
The two-day meeting is attended by 33 branch managers in Japan and BOJ officials stationed in London, New York and Hong Kong.
